title: Source-checked repair with preserved analysis history
changes: Check literal source-fact claims against authoritative source evidence before relying on AI review.
Distinguish AI-reviewed sections from sections that passed deterministic source checks.
Permit one explicitly approved targeted repair and independent re-review while preserving the original responses.
Resolve proven duplicate context declarations and exact property aliases with separately reviewed evidence.
Append checkpoint-bound continuation records without replacing earlier approvals or restarting the whole file.
Continue remaining work only after corrective checks pass; stop on rejection, malformed output or uncertain operations.
limitations: Server-side preparation must be configured and tested by the operator; a source release does not enable it.
This hosted preparation route accepts one FMB per request; MMB, OLB and PLL require the separate supported preparation route.
The focused prototype profile, current authority endpoint and private browser worker require explicit operator configuration and live checks.
Real-file OPAF-to-APEX import, authenticated runtime and downloadable export acceptance remain pending.
A corrected candidate requires new independent review; an earlier approval does not certify changed content or override a failed source check.
Repair is limited to the approved checkpoint plan before database stages. There is no automatic corrective loop or replay of uncertain calls or imports.
Technical identifiers are retained; redaction receipts are not complete PII certification or processing permission.
APEX generated, technical checks passed and business acceptance remain separate.
A prototype export does not prove clean-schema reimport, customer-target compatibility or business equivalence.
Release notes describe software changes, not proof of a successful conversion.
